# dsdot

> Computes the inner product of two vectors with extended precision accumulation and result.

<section class="usage">

## Usage

```js
import dsdot from '@rreusser/blahpack/blas/dsdot';
```

### Layout API

Takes a storage layout (`order`) and leading dimensions, like CBLAS/LAPACKE.

```js
dsdot( N, x, strideX, y, strideY ) → number
```

| Parameter | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `N` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Number of elements in input vector(s) |
| `x` | `Float64Array`<br><sub>length N</sub> | First input vector, with N elements (accumulated in double precision). |
| ↳ `strideX` | `integer` | Stride length for `x` |
| `y` | `Float64Array`<br><sub>length N</sub> | Second input vector, with N elements. |
| ↳ `strideY` | `integer` | Stride length for `y` |

<details>
<summary>Reference notes for each argument (the reference implementation's own documentation; 1-based indices)</summary>

- `N`: number of elements in input vector(s)
- `x`: single precision vector with N elements
- `y`: single precision vector with N elements

</details>

**Returns** `number`: dot product

### Strided (ndarray) API

Takes explicit strides and offsets for every array. Use it for views, sub-matrices and non-unit strides.

```js
dsdot.ndarray( N, x, strideX, offsetX, y, strideY, offsetY ) → number
```

Computes the dot product of two vectors with extended precision accumulation.

| Parameter | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `N` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Number of indexed elements |
| `x` | `Float64Array`<br><sub>length N</sub> | First input array |
| ↳ `strideX` | `integer` | `x` stride length |
| ↳ `offsetX` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Starting `x` index |
| `y` | `Float64Array`<br><sub>length N</sub> | Second input array |
| ↳ `strideY` | `integer` | `y` stride length |
| ↳ `offsetY` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Starting `y` index |

<details>
<summary>Reference notes for each argument (the reference implementation's own documentation; 1-based indices)</summary>

- `N`: number of elements in input vector(s)
- `x`: single precision vector with N elements
- `y`: single precision vector with N elements

</details>

**Returns** `number`: dot product

</section>

## Notes

-   `dsdot()` corresponds to the reference BLAS routine [`DSDOT`](https://github.com/Reference-LAPACK/lapack/blob/v3.12.0/BLAS/SRC/dsdot.f).

<section class="examples">

## Examples

```js
import Float64Array from '@stdlib/array/float64/lib/index.js';
import dsdot from './../lib/base.js';

// Compute the dot product with extended precision:
const x = new Float64Array( [ 1.0, 2.0, 3.0 ] );
const y = new Float64Array( [ 4.0, 5.0, 6.0 ] );

const result = dsdot( 3, x, 1, 0, y, 1, 0 );
console.log( result ); // eslint-disable-line no-console
// => 32.0
```

</section>

<!-- /.examples -->

<section class="reference-notes">

## Reference notes

The mathematical description from the reference BLAS 3.12.0 source of `DSDOT`. Indices are the 1-based Fortran indices of the source.

### Purpose

Compute the inner product of two vectors with extended precision accumulation and result.

Returns D.P. dot product accumulated in D.P., for S.P. `SX` and `SY` DSDOT = sum for $I = 0$ to N-1 of $\mathrm{SX}(\mathrm{LX}+I \, \mathrm{INCX}) \, \mathrm{SY}(\mathrm{LY}+I \, \mathrm{INCY})$, where $\mathrm{LX} = 1$ if `INCX` .GE. 0, else $\mathrm{LX} = 1+(1-N) \, \mathrm{INCX}$, and LY is defined in a similar way using `INCY`.

### References

C. L. Lawson, R. J. Hanson, D. R. Kincaid and F. T. Krogh, Basic linear algebra subprograms for Fortran usage, Algorithm No. 539, Transactions on Mathematical Software 5, 3 (September 1979), pp. 308-323.
